rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No stale markers, no "fixed" retrospectives, no session biography.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L21 maintainer block ('The lede simulates a named file...', 2026-08-14, Antti-worded) reads: "It breaks a chain that was genuinely broken: the lecture used to assert 'You have a .md file with three to five rules', which extract-the-task-shaping-rule stopped guaranteeing when it let the student place rules anywhere on the load map ... and an earlier standalone task-shaping .md was removed on purpose." Confirmed live: grep -inE '\bused to\b|\bstopped\b|\bwas removed\b' over the maintainer+backing region (awk from <!-- maintainer -->) hits exactly this line. 'used to' is named verbatim in the rule's own tell list; 'stopped guaranteeing' and 'was removed on purpose' are the same transition-verb shape as the rule's own worked examples ('used to sit in X', 'X was changed to Y'). Harm: this is the rule's central target -- a maintainer note narrating HOW the design got here (a prior lecture assertion, a second exercise's change, a file's removal) rather than stating what binds now; it will rot the moment extract-the-task-shaping-rule's own wiring moves again, since nothing here is flagged do-not-reintroduce. Not fully a false positive: the mechanical mechanical mechanical-grep the rule supplies (tell-word + bare year within 80 chars) returns 0 hits on this clause because no year sits near 'used to' here, which is exactly the case the rule warns the grep alone would miss ('the grep cannot catch a verb'). One clause survives as a keepable empirical finding: 'most land in an existing CLAUDE.md / CLAUDE.local.md' is present-tense and load-bearing (explains why the lede can't assume the student has a concrete file) -- only the journey wrapped around it (used to / stopped / was removed) is the violation.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Keep the present-tense empirical finding ('most rules land in an existing CLAUDE.md / CLAUDE.local.md, not a dedicated file') and the dated attribution header; cut the transition-verb chain around it ('the lecture used to assert X, which Y stopped guaranteeing ... an earlier file was removed on purpose') and state instead why the hypothetical file exists now, not how the prior design changed into this one.
